study type: Retrospective case-control study (for risk factors) and quasi-experimental study (for treatment comparison)
exposure: Electromyography biofeedback (EB) combined with neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NES)
outcome: International Consultation Committee on Incontinence Questionnaire Short Form (ICI-Q-SF) scores (quality of life)
cohort: The study included 180 patients with postpartum stress urinary incontinence (PSUI) and 80 patients without PSUI for risk factor analysis, with the 180 PSUI patients subsequently divided into two groups for treatment comparison.
finding: Vaginal delivery, urinary incontinence before pregnancy, new urinary incontinence in pregnancy, and delivery of a large infant were identified as risk factors for PSUI, and electromyography biofeedback combined with neuromuscular electrical stimulation was more effective than Kegel kinesiotherapy in treating PSUI.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was identified as a risk factor for postpartum stress urinary incontinence (PSUI).
